findings.summary: The numbered sections run 6 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 across the part, so the reader meets section 6 before section 1.
findings.evidence: Page 1 heading order: "6. First Five Mistakes", then "1. Getting Work Back", then "2. Traps With Merges"; page 2 continues "3. Pick Your Tool", "4. Configure Once", "5. Recovery Reflex".
findings.fix: Renumber the six sections in reading order: 1. First Five Mistakes, 2. Getting Work Back, 3. Traps With Merges, 4. Pick Your Tool, 5. Configure Once, 6. Recovery Reflex.

findings.summary: The claim that only uncommitted work can be destroyed is false and directly contradicts the reflog-expiry bullet two lines above it.
findings.evidence: "Uncommitted work is the only work you can destroy" — immediately preceded by "Reflog keeps reachable entries ~90 days, but rebase/reset orphans only ~30 (`gc.reflogExpireUnreachable`) — recover **soon**, not eventually."
findings.fix: Reword to scope the claim, e.g. "Committed work survives until its reflog entry expires; uncommitted work has no safety net at all" — and note that `git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc --prune=now` destroys committed work immediately.

findings.summary: The second half of the "Pick Your Tool" decision table is stranded under the unrelated "4. Configure Once" heading, after a config code block.
findings.evidence: "4. Configure Once" + the four `git config` lines are followed by a table with the same headers as section 3 — ["Situation","Reach for"] with rows such as ["need one commit only","cherry-pick -x <sha>"] and ["built on the wrong base","rebase --onto new old br"].
findings.fix: Move that continuation table up so it directly follows the first ["Situation","Reach for"] table under "3. Pick Your Tool", leaving only the config code block under "4. Configure Once".

findings.summary: The pre-commit hook's `git grep` inspects the working tree instead of the staged snapshot, so it checks content that is not being committed.
findings.evidence: "if git grep -qn '^<<<<<<< '; then" in the `.git/hooks/pre-commit` snippet
findings.fix: Use `git grep --cached -q '^<<<<<<< '` so the hook tests the index, matching the `git diff --cached --check` line above it (which, note, already flags leftover conflict markers on its own).

findings.summary: Section 6 is printed before sections 1 and 2, so the numbering does not match the reading order.
findings.evidence: Page 1 heading order: "6. First Five Mistakes", then "1. Getting Work Back", then "2. Traps With Merges"; page 2 continues "3.", "4.", "5."
findings.fix: Either move the mistakes block after section 5 on page 2, or renumber the headings so the printed order runs 1 through 6.

findings.summary: The pre-commit hook offered as the fix for committing conflict markers inspects the working tree rather than what is staged, so it does not verify the claim it supports.
findings.evidence: Table row "committed conflict markers | hook + git diff --check" supported by "if git grep -qn '^<<<<<<< '; then" inside `.git/hooks/pre-commit`.
findings.fix: Use `git grep --cached -qn '^<<<<<<< '` (or drop the grep, since `git diff --cached --check` on the line above already flags markers in the staged content).

findings.summary: The last line of the "Configure Once" block omits `--global`, so it silently applies only to the current repository.
findings.evidence: "git config merge.conflictStyle zdiff3" following three lines that all use `git config --global`

findings.summary: The "Recovery Reflex" bullets contradict each other: one says orphaned commits expire in ~30 days, the next says only uncommitted work can be destroyed.
findings.evidence: "Reflog keeps reachable entries ~90 days, but rebase/reset orphans only ~30 (`gc.reflogExpireUnreachable`) — recover **soon**, not eventually." followed immediately by "Uncommitted work is the only work you can destroy".
findings.fix: Qualify the last bullet, e.g. "Uncommitted work is the only work you can destroy instantly — committed work dies only when its reflog entry expires".

findings.summary: The "Configure Once" block sets merge.conflictStyle without --global, so it does not do what the section title and the cheat-sheet row promise.
findings.evidence: "git config --global rerere.enabled true" … then "git config merge.conflictStyle zdiff3" (no --global), while the decision table says "confused which side | merge.conflictStyle zdiff3" and Part 1 states "# set --global; never guess intent again".
findings.fix: Change the line to `git config --global merge.conflictStyle zdiff3`.
